text: Third Day is a Christian rock band formed in Marietta, Georgia in 1991 by lead singer Mac Powell, guitarist Mark Lee, and pianist Billy Wilkins. The band's name references the biblical resurrection of Jesus on the third day after his crucifixion. In 1992, they performed at a church event with the Bullard Family Singers, featuring David Carr and Tai Anderson, who were later invited to join the band. In 1993, they began playing regularly in the Atlanta area to fund album recording; Wilkins left to pursue teaching. Their debut album, Long Time Forgotten, was recorded at Furies Studios with production help from Carr and sold 2,000 copies. In 1994, they added August McCoy as a second guitarist and released the self-financed album Contagious for $3,000, which included 1,000 CDs and cassettes; McCoy left that year to attend college. At a show in Marietta, they signed with Gray Dot Records, releasing the album Third Day that sold 20,000 copies; Reunion Records later bought the contract and signed them for a multi-album deal. In 1995, Brad Avery joined after auditioning and playing "Consuming Fire," and the official version of Third Day was released, selling over 300,000 copies and earning a mainstream rock hit, "Nothing at All," which reached No. 34 on the Billboard rock charts. The band opened for Newsboys on five West Coast shows and launched a 65-city tour with All Star United and Seven Day Jesus. In 1996, they were nominated for a Dove Award for New Artist of the Year and won a Billboard Music Award for the "Consuming Fire" video, shot in Bombay Beach and around the Salton Sea, which later inspired the artwork for Revelation. In 1997, they began work on Conspiracy No. 5 with producer Sam Taylor, which was Grammy-nominated and won Dove Awards for Rock Album of the Year and Rock Song of the Year ("Alien"). In 1998, they worked with Monroe Jones, whose produced album Time was Grammy-nominated and won a Dove Award; songs left out were released on the EP Southern Tracks. They released Offerings: A Worship Album, recorded in a week, and toured with Jennifer Knapp in 2000. That year, they also collaborated on City on a Hill: Songs of Worship and Praise with FFH, Caedmon's Call, SonicFlood, Jars of Clay, and others. In 2001, they toured Australia and New Zealand following the success of Offerings and recorded a concert with 15,000 fans at the HiFi Buys Amphitheatre, released as The Offerings Experience. The year also saw them win five Dove Awards and their first Grammy, with the album Come Together winning two Dove Awards and a Grammy, and being certified gold the following year. The band appeared in the 2002 film Joshua, with "My Hope is You" included in the soundtrack. In 2003, they released Offerings II: All I Have to Give. In 2004, they released Wire, toured with tobyMac and Warren Barfield, and went to Europe for a two-week tour; they recorded a live concert in Louisville and released it as Live Wire. They also contributed to the soundtrack of Mel Gibson's The Passion of the Christ, played at the Republican National Convention, and were featured on 60 Minutes. In January 2007, they performed in Melbourne, Brisbane, and Sydney, Australia. Their album Wherever You Are debuted at No. 8 on the Billboard 200 and won their third Grammy. In 2006, they released their first Christmas-themed album, Christmas Offerings, and in 2007, their first hits compilation, Chronology. On February 28, 2008, Brad Avery announced his departure after 13 years and over 1,000 concerts to pursue solo projects, and the band continued as a quartet. They performed at the 2008 Papal Youth Rally in Yonkers, N.Y. In support of the July 29, 2008, release of Revelation, they performed on The Tonight Show with Jay Leno and The Late Late Show with Craig Ferguson. "Call My Name" reached No. 1 and was the fifth most-played song on R&R's Christian CHR chart in 2008. In April 2009, they released Live Revelations, a live version of Revelation, and were inducted into the Georgia Music Hall of Fame on September 19, 2009. Live Revelations won the Grammy for Best Rock or Rap Gospel Album, their fourth Grammy, and was certified Gold, becoming their eighth Gold album. In 2010, they appeared at Winter Jam with the Newsboys, Fireflight, and Tenth Avenue North, released the single "Lift Up Your Face," and released their tenth studio album, Move, on October 19. They concluded the Make a Difference Tour 2010 with TobyMac, Michael W. Smith, Jason Gray, and Max Lucado in Fayetteville, NC. The song "Follow Me There" from Move became the theme song for the TLC show Sarah Palin's Alaska, which debuted in 2010. In 2012, they released Miracle, touring with Colton Dixon and Josh Wilson from February 21, 2013, to May 19, 2014. In 2015, they released the worship album Lead Us Back: Songs of Worship, produced by The Sound Kids, which peaked at No. 20 on the Billboard 200, No. 1 on the Christian Albums chart, No. 5 on the Top Rock Albums chart, and No. 13 on the Digital Albums chart; the single "Soul on Fire" spent 19 weeks on the Billboard charts, peaking at No. 2 on Hot Christian Songs and No. 3 on Christian Digital Songs. In 2015, bassist Tai Anderson announced a break from touring after 23 years with the band. To celebrate their 25th anniversary, they released their thirteenth and final album, Revival, on August 4, 2017, recorded at FAME Studios in Muscle Shoals, Alabama, and reunited with producer Monroe Jones. On March 2, 2018, the band announced a farewell tour with 12 shows, later expanded to 20 concerts, with the final show in Denver on June 27, 2018. In June 2025, they announced a reunion with the lineup of Mac Powell, Mark Lee, David Carr, and Tai Anderson to celebrate their 30th anniversary, with a limited tour beginning in spring 2026. As of 2020, the band has earned 4 Grammy Awards and 25 Dove Awards. They have sold over 7 million albums in the United States and had 28 number one Christian album chart hits. Their fans are known as "Gomers" after a song on their second album about Gomer. The band was inducted into the Georgia Music Hall of Fame on September 19, 2009.
